dedupe_keys.name: new south wales exercise paton a statewide simulation of emergency department response to pandemic influenza 2006

description: This case study reports Exercise Paton, a statewide simulation exercise run in New South Wales, Australia, on 30 November 2006. It tested how emergency departments, multi-purpose services and public health units would respond to single patients presenting with pandemic influenza in the early stages of a pandemic. The exercise followed the release of the state policy Hospital Response to Pandemic Influenza, Part 1: Emergency Department Response, and was named after Dr Robert Paton, Director-General of Public Health during the 1918 to 1919 influenza pandemic. Adam T. Craig and Paul Armstrong of the NSW Department of Health described it in Communicable Diseases Intelligence in 2007. The article is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives licence. Coverage is the whole state health system. Caveats: an exercise tests plans and procedures, not real surge conditions, and scenario details and findings must be read in the full article. Simulation uses: a documented exercise design and early pandemic case scenario for validating hospital infection control and surge procedures in emergency department models. Related records: the Stavanger emergency department COVID-19 simulation (case_study-stavanger-emergency-department-covid-patient-flow-hybrid-simulation) models pandemic rules in one department, and NHSN hospital respiratory data (data-cdc-nhsn-hospital-respiratory-data) track real respiratory surges.
